characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 3 h has a Vickers hardness of 863.9 ± 15.8 HV (Table 4); the 19Al solution-treated baseline is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Vickers load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, hardness given as average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 19Al samples

characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al alloy composition measured by EDS: Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure alloy chemical composition and elemental distribution

characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD patterns (Fig. 10) show α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn for the aged alloys.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: SE images (Fig. 9) show the α → β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy is thermally activated and slow; β-Mn decorates α grain boundaries at 550 °C and higher.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in aged samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm (low mag) and 0.05 μm (high mag)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); after high-temperature aging the 19Al alloy phase map is almost entirely β-Mn (Fig. 6), with new FCC (600 °C/3 h) and BCC (650 °C/6 h) precipitates.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and their distribution in aged alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins form at β-Mn interfaces in the peak-hardness alloys.
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate microstructures (β-Mn, FCC Cu-rich phase) of ultra-high hardness alloys
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS

interfaces.interface_notes: The FCC Cu-rich phase forms due to the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys and the expulsion of Cu from β-Mn during precipitation/growth; the BCC phase forms at the β-Mn interfaces owing to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing Al around the β-Mn interfaces. Interfaces were characterized in the peak-hardness 15Al (600 °C/6 h) and 17Al (575 °C/6 h) samples by TEM, not specifically at 625 °C/3 h.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (general microstructure evolution during aging of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere; alloy designated 19Al.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching (parent state of the aged sample).
Solution-treated 19Al sample aged at 625 °C for 3 h followed by water quenching; corresponds to the 625 °C aging / 3 h entry of Table 4 for the 19Al alloy.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester; Vickers load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and hardness given as average of 5 measurements.
Density measured by Archimedes method; elastic modulus measured through compressive stress-strain curves.

phases_present.morphology: matrix formed by near-complete α → β-Mn transformation (aged at ≥600 °C)
fine particles at β-Mn interfaces, containing FCC twins

precipitates.distribution: at interfaces between the β-Mn (within β-Mn)

structures.overall_structure: For the 19Al alloy aged at temperatures of 600 °C and above, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging, with numerous fine precipitates distributed within the β-Mn; the 625 °C / 3 h condition therefore falls in this regime (α almost completely transformed to β-Mn). The ultra-hard aged 19Al alloy is composed of β-Mn together with BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases distributed between the β-Mn interfaces.

unmapped_findings: The as-solution-treated (pre-aging) baseline of the 19Al alloy is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV, reported once across all aging-temperature rows of Table 4; this defines the starting hardness of the sample before the 625 °C / 3 h aging.

For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high hardness is reported as 575 °C–625 °C, so this sample's 625 °C aging lies within that optimal window (with 3 h giving 863.9 ± 15.8 HV).

The temperature-dependent hardness plateau for the 19Al alloy at 625 °C aging across times is ~855–871 HV (855.6 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 863.9 ± 15.8 HV at 3 h, 870.7 ± 16.1 HV at 6 h, 869.5 ± 8.6 HV at 10 h), i.e. essentially time-independent at this temperature.

General conclusion (b0079): increasing the Al content slightly enhances the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn but also decreases the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces and decreases the fracture toughness of the ultra-hard alloys, reducing the final hardening effect.

General statement (b0053): for the 19Al alloy at temperatures of 600 °C and above, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging, with numerous fine precipitates distributed within the β-Mn.
